record.original_question: Let Ω be an open connected subset of C^n, and let Γ: Ω -> C^n be a holomorphic mapping such that the maximal rank of its Jacobian DΓ is an integer k with 1 <= k <= n - 1. For each point ξ in the maximal-rank set Ω^(k) = {ξ in Ω : rank DΓ(ξ) = k}, assume the level set Γ^{-1}(Γ(ξ)) is an affine (n-k)-dimensional space through ξ, equivalently of the form ξ + κ(ξ) where κ(ξ) = ker DΓ(ξ). Under these hypotheses, when does the resulting affine fibration extend analytically from Ω^(k) to all of Ω?

evidence.quote: (A1) Let us denote k := max ξ∈Ω rank DΓ(ξ) and assume that 1 ≤ k ≤ n − 1. Let Ω(k) denote the set of ξ where the rank of DΓ is maximal, i.e. Ω(k) = {ξ ∈ Ω : rank DΓ(ξ) = k}. (A2) Assume that for every ξ ∈ Ω(k), the level set Γ−1(Γ(ξ)) = {η ∈ Ω : Γ(η) = Γ(ξ)} is an affine (n − k)–dimensional space through ξ.

We note that condition (A2) implies that for ξ ∈ Ω(k) we have Γ−1(Γ(ξ)) = ξ + κ(ξ), so that the dependence of the level sets on ξ ∈ Ω(k) is analytic. The main question of this paper is when (and whether) this fibration extends analytically from Ω(k) to the set Ω.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be an open connected subset, and let $\Gamma : \Omega 	o \mathbb{C}^n$ be a holomorphic mapping. Define
$$k := \max_{\xi \in \Omega} \operatorname{rank} D\Gamma(\xi),$$
and assume $1 \le k \le n-1$. Let
$$\Omega^{(k)} := \{\xi \in \Omega : \operatorname{rank} D\Gamma(\xi) = k\},$$
which is an open dense subset of $\Omega$. Assume the following geometric condition:

(A) For every $\xi \in \Omega^{(k)}$, the level set
$$\Gamma^{-1}(\Gamma(\xi)) = \{\eta \in \Omega : \Gamma(\eta) = \Gamma(\xi)\}$$
is an affine $(n-k)$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{C}^n$ passing through $\xi$; equivalently, $\Gamma^{-1}(\Gamma(\xi)) \cap \Omega = (\xi + \kappa(\xi)) \cap \Omega$, where $\kappa(\xi) := \ker D\Gamma(\xi)$.

Under these hypotheses, the assignment $\xi \mapsto \xi + \kappa(\xi)$ defines an analytic affine fibration of $\Omega^{(k)}$ by $(n-k)$-planes. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which this affine fibration extends analytically from $\Omega^{(k)}$ to all of $\Omega$, in the sense that there exists a holomorphic mapping $\xi \mapsto L(\xi)$ on $\Omega$, with values in the Grassmannian-affine bundle of $(n-k)$-dimensional affine subspaces of $\mathbb{C}^n$, such that $L(\xi) = \xi + \kappa(\xi)$ for all $\xi \in \Omega^{(k)}$. In particular, does such an extension always exist, and if not, characterize the obstructions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem in complex analytic geometry motivated by regularity theory of Fourier integral operators. A subsequent survey by the same author ("Singularities of affine fibrations in the regularity theory of Fourier integral operators") still discusses this as an open problem with only partial results, and no later publication appears to claim a complete resolution.

status_evidence.title: Singularities of affine fibrations in the regularity theory of Fourier integral operators (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing affine fibrations arising from holomorphic maps with constant-rank stratum, presenting partial results and open conjectures on analytic extension.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of analytically extending the affine fibration from the maximal-rank stratum to all of Ω is treated as an open problem with only partial answers.

status_evidence.title: An open problem in complex analytic geometry arising in harmonic analysis (arXiv:0711.0605)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper formulates an open problem and a conjecture about the structure of affine fibrations associated with holomorphic mappings.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an open problem accompanied by a conjecture, not as a theorem.
